title: aidd context --json
description: What `aidd context --json` prints (experimental): the minimal context for one step of a Spec, as what to read, never the contents. Each token estimate is the text's characters divided by four.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape. A new key keeps it; a renamed, removed, or retyped key bumps it.

role.description: The role the pack is for (`--role`), or null for every role.

step.description: The step code the pack is for (`--step`), or null.

items.description: What the step reads, in reading order.

tokens.description: The items' token estimates, added up.

head.description: The commit the pack was made at, so a pack made before a later commit reads as stale.

spec_hash.description: The Spec hash of the working tree's Spec and the files it freezes, as `aidd hash --worktree` prints it, so a pack made before the Spec changed reads as stale.

kind.description: What the item is. `playbook` is the role's agent file, first, when the lead plays the role itself (`--play`). `living` is product-level work the role keeps or builds against, such as the architecture overview or the product prototype (`loop.documents`: its owner and `read_by`). `test`, `acceptance`, `evidence`, `command`, and `threat-model` are a loop step's own reads (`loop.step_reads`): a `command` names one to run, such as `aidd test` or the diff's stat.

command.description: The command to run: the summary's, or a step's, such as `aidd gate --spec <path>`.

reason.description: One line: why the step reads it.

tokens.description: About how many tokens reading it costs.
